issues.problem: DEC-69 (2026-11-01) rules that the cex's Troyanov theorem (MR1005085) is 'a named external result with a non-vacuity witness, the row partial (an exception to DEC-23)'. kb/0012 is the pattern: a named hypothesis plus a proved witness that the hypothesis set is satisfiable. The file does neither. REPORT says 'The named hypothesis is not stated here', and SCOPE (c) says 'no named Troyanov hypothesis is stated'. The cex is carried only as two anonymous hypotheses, hrigid and hrot, of an abstract inference. Nothing shows they can hold together with O ∈ sing M. They are not easy to satisfy. hrigid fails at any finite-order branch point (a cone of angle 2πk has local deck rotations at O), so the obvious small witnesses are excluded, and the theorem as stated may be vacuous. The row is correctly 'partial' and unmarked, so nothing is overclaimed. But the ruling's prescribed form is missing. That is a missing assertion, not a style point.
issues.fix: Implement DEC-69 in the kb/0012 shape. (a) A named Prop packaging the external input, for example GX.TroyanovSuspensionFacts G X M O := O ∈ Sing G X M ∧ hrigid ∧ hrot. Optionally add a named Prop for the (SO(4),S³) existence statement over the angle condition 0 < Σ(θ_i − 2π) + 4π ≤ min(4π, θ_i). (b) isAnalyticModelFamily_unit_iff_eq_singleton restated from it. (c) A non-vacuity witness, at the level the master accepts: at minimum, a proved instance of the angle condition with s = 3 pairwise distinct θ_i (the premise of Troyanov's theorem is non-empty); preferably a singular (G,X)-manifold with a point satisfying hrigid and hrot. If even (a) is judged unstatable because spherical cone surfaces are not in the library, raise an OQ asking whether the abstract inference plus SCOPE (c) discharges DEC-69. Do not leave the ruling silently unapplied.

superseded_audit_1.summary: Builds: taskset -c 0-11 lake env lean exits 0 in about 5 s. There is exactly one 'declaration uses sorry' warning, at l.879 (GX.isVirtuallyTame_of_isXAManifold), which matches REPORT sorry_count 1. #print axioms, run through stdin so nothing was written, shows sorryAx only under GX.local_virt_tame. These are all clean (propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound): forall_isTame_iff, hasType_unique, isTamifyingTopology_natural_iff, IsTamifyingTopology.induced_reg_eq, exists_lift_singularAut, isVirtuallyTame_of_isXAManifold_of_isTame, isAnalyticModelFamily_iff, ModelChart.exists_aut_eq. No declaration name clashes with GX/ or scaffold/: all 50 were grepped. Fidelity of the six marked definitions holds. singularAut is the subgroup of homeomorphisms that are a.e. morphisms, with inverses by symm_of_homeomorph. IsAnalyticModelFamily is split into two fields, and isAnalyticModelFamily_iff proves it equivalent to the printed single clause with the cast. ModelChart / HasType / IsModelAtlas / IsXAManifold follow the paper literally: x in sing(M) is derived (ModelChart.mem_sing), and the charts' domains cover M. IsTamifyingTopology has (A)-(D) and the side conditions. T is used as a local instance only where intended: IsRegDevelopingOnReg, deckMapsMax and aeAutMapsMax are defined outside the T-context, and coinduced and IsPortly are explicit. The definition is not trivial: the discrete topology fails (A). IsLocallyGaloisian uses DEC-55's literal IsSLSCInCC on each open U with its induced structure. theo:local_virt_tame is stated faithfully and REPORT says honestly that it is 'stated'. (i)=>(ii) is proved, and the agent correctly notes the theorem is degenerate: HasAutContinuousTamifying already gives (ii). The tame-model case and three proof steps are proved without sorry. The partial rows rem:singular_point_manifold_has and rem:theorem_theo_local_tame are unmarked in the module docstring. Their findings check out against l.1921-1926: the remark's proof gives only uniqueness, and the per-manifold 'only if' is false. The finding on the proof at l.2101-2103 is plausible. It concerns overlapping chart domains near a singular point that is the centre of neither chart, possibly with two different types: analyticity does not apply there, and the generated topology is a join. It is the right question for the author. Two issues are major. First, cex:start_singular_manifold_homeomorphic was dispatched as 'cited - prove' and is neither proved nor stated: there is no declaration and no tagged sorry, against 'state first' and DEC-23 (same pattern as WP-26f's audit). Second, the theo:local_virt_tame sorry rests on an unbuilt lemma, not on a mathematical obstruction, although the dispatch said 'prove in full'. The minor issues: bold marks on partial labels in declaration docstrings; one REPORT hypotheses entry mislabelled; DEC-27 counterexamples not formalized for the two partial remarks; the ledger will attribute the file's one sorry to every marked label in the file.

issues.problem: The dispatch lists this row as 'cited - prove'. DEC-23 says cited results are built, not assumed. The file contains no Lean statement of it: no declaration, no tagged sorry. It has only the abstract last inference, IsAnalyticModelFamily.inter_eq_empty_of_not_extend, which is the contrapositive of the definition and says nothing about M, Sigma or {O}. The obstruction given is real: there are no spherical cone surfaces, no Troyanov MR1005085 (a PDE existence theorem) and no (SO(4),S^3) suspension structure. But the protocol wants the statement written down, with a tagged sorry on the missing ingredients, so that the obstruction lies in the file rather than only in prose. REPORT is honest about it, so nothing is overclaimed. This is the same pattern WP-26f's audit rated major.
issues.fix: Either state the counterexample with tagged sorries as far as the library allows, or ask the master session or the author to scope it. Possible abstractions: (a) a hypothesis-free statement parametrised by a singular (G,X)-manifold M with a point O and a structure Aut(M) = {id} on every neighbourhood of O, concluding '(M,S) analytic iff S = {O}'; (b) an author ruling, analogous to DEC-26's scoping, on whether Troyanov's theorem is built or carried as a named external. Until then, record the row as blocked on that ruling in REPORT/notes.

issues.problem: The dispatch says 'prove in full'. The one sorry is justified by 'lem:spread_top (l.1989) is outside this dispatch and not built'. That is a missing lemma, not a mathematical obstruction. CAMPAIGN.md says to prove a lemma you need in your own file, and lem:spread_top is assigned to no package (no other campaign directory or scaffold file mentions it). No partial reduction was attempted either: lem:spread_top is not stated, even with a tagged sorry, and the theorem's proof is not assembled from it. So the sorry covers the whole (ii)=>(i) construction, not one cited step. Mitigation: the agent found a plausible gap in the gluing step (l.2101-2103). Under the literal def:atlas reading, it may make the statement unprovable without an author ruling. That part is a genuine obstruction and was reported correctly as a question.
issues.fix: First, get the author's ruling on the def:atlas reading (question 1 below). Then either (a) dispatch lem:spread_top (and def:topological_spaces_continuous_map, l.1984) as its own package and close the theorem from it, or (b) in this file, state lem:spread_top in the strong/weak two-topology form the proof consumes, with SORRY(lem:spread_top), and prove (ii)=>(i) from it. If the ruling keeps the literal reading and the gap cannot be closed, apply DEC-27: give the strongest true form (for example, every singular point is a chart centre) and a counterexample, or keep the row partial.
